questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:**

The judge ruled ____ favor of the plaintiff after reviewing all the evidence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. in .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is about the judge's ruling in favor of the plaintiff, so the correct preposition to use is **"in."**
 
• The phrase "in favor of" is a fixed expression commonly used to indicate support or a decision made for someone or something.
 
• Other prepositions such as "at," "for," and "into" do not fit the context of this sentence and would render it grammatically incorrect.

Correct sentence: *The judge ruled **in** favor of the plaintiff after reviewing all the evidence*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common usage of "in favor of":**
 
 
• **Example:** The committee voted **in favor of** the new policy.
 
• **Meaning:** Indicates agreement or support for something.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect usage of other prepositions:**
 
 
• "at favor of" or "into favor of" are not valid expressions.
 
• "for favor of" might seem logical but is not grammatically correct in standard English.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The student said that the teacher had explained the lesson clearly.

options.text: The student said, "The teacher explained the lesson clearly."
The student said, "The teacher has explained the lesson clearly."
The student said, "The teacher had explained the lesson clearly."
The student said, "The teacher explains the lesson clearly, "

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. The student said, "The teacher has explained the lesson clearly." .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **indirect speech**, and the task is to convert it into **direct speech**.
 
• In indirect speech, the past perfect tense (**had explained**) turns into present perfect tense (**has explained**) when converted to direct speech.
 
• The correct option is **Option 2:** The student said, "The teacher has explained the lesson clearly."

Correct sentence: *The student said, "The teacher has explained the lesson clearly."*.

• Quotation marks (**" "**) are used to enclose the statement.
 
• Ensure the reporting verb (**said**) is followed by a comma before the quoted speech.

• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it uses the simple past tense (*explained*), which changes the tense.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because it uses the past perfect tense (*had explained*), which is inconsistent with the original tense.

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The CEO is expected to have brought about significant changes in the department by the end of the year.

options.text: Significant changes are expected to have been brought about in the department by the new CEO by the end of the year.
It is expected that significant changes will have been brought about in the department by the new CEO by the end of the year.
Significant changes will have been brought about in the department by the new CEO by the end of the year.
The new CEO is expected that significant changes will be brought about by them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1', i.e. Significant changes are expected to have been brought about in the department by the new CEO by the end of the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice: **The CEO is expected to have brought about significant changes in the department by the end of the year.**
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
 
• Here, "Significant changes" are the object of the active voice sentence, so they become the subject in the passive voice.
 
• The correct structure for passive voice transformation in this case is: **Object + is/are + expected + to have been + past participle.**

Correct sentence: *Significant changes are expected to have been brought about in the department by the new CEO by the end of the year.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active to Passive Voice Transformation Rules:**

 
 
• The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb form changes to include the verb "to be" + past participle.
 
• The subject of the active sentence becomes the agent in the passive sentence (introduced by "by").
 
 
 
• In this case, "The CEO" is the agent, and "Significant changes" is the object turned subject in the passive voice.

questions.question: In the sentence: "The deep ocean remains one of the least explored parts of our planet," what is the **tense **of the verb "**remains**"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "**remains**" is in the **Present Simple** tense.
 
• In English, the Present Simple is used to state **facts, general truths, or permanent situations**. The fact that the deep ocean is unexplored is a current, ongoing reality.
 
• Grammatically, "remains" is the third-person singular form of the root verb "remain." It follows the structure: **Subject + Verb (s/es)**.
 
• The word count for the provided passage is approximately **155 words**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence Analysis:** *"The deep ocean (Subject) **remains** (Present Simple Verb) one of the least explored parts..."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Past Perfect** – This would require "had remained." It describes an action completed before another point in the past.
 
• **Option 3: Present Continuous** – This would require "is remaining." It describes an action happening exactly at the moment of speaking.
 
• **Option 4: Future Simple** – This would require "will remain." It describes an action that has not yet happened.

questions.question: In the sentence: "Some deep-sea creatures, like certain jellyfish, glow in the dark through a chemical reaction in their bodies," is the sentence in **active or passive voice**?

options.text: Active voice - “ the subject performs the action
Passive voice - the action is done to the subject
Passive voice - the agent is unknown
Active voice - no verb is used

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Active Voice**, the subject of the sentence performs the action expressed by the verb.
 
• In this sentence, the subject is "**Some deep-sea creatures**" (specifically, certain jellyfish). The action they are performing is "**glow**."
 
• Because the subjects themselves are performing the action of glowing, rather than having the action performed upon them, the sentence is in the active voice.
 
• The word count for the provided passage is **155 words**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Voice Analysis:** *"Some deep-sea creatures (Subject) + glow (Action/Verb) + in the dark..."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 & 3: Passive Voice** – These are incorrect because the sentence does not use a "to be" verb + past participle (e.g., "Light is produced by..."). In passive voice, the subject receives the action.
 
• **Option 4: Active voice - no verb** – This is a contradiction. Every sentence must have a verb, and in this case, "glow" is the active verb.

• In the context of the passage, it refers to the ability of deep-sea creatures, like the **anglerfish** and certain **jellyfish**, to produce and emit light through chemical reactions within their bodies.

questions.question: Which of the following words refers to a strong and deep hatred of something?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Antipathy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "Antipathy" refers to a deep-seated feeling of dislike or aversion, which can be synonymous with a strong and deep hatred of something.
 
• **Envy:** Refers to a desire for what someone else has, not a form of hatred.
 
• **Empathy:** Refers to the ability to understand and share the feelings of another, not related to hatred.
 
• **Sympathy:** Refers to feelings of pity and sorrow for someone else's misfortune, not related to hatred.
 
• Thus, the correct option is **Antipathy**.

Correct sentence: *"Which of the following words refers to a strong and deep hatred of something?" The answer is **Antipathy.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antipathy:** Often used to describe an intense dislike or aversion to something specific. For example: "He felt a strong antipathy towards dishonesty."
 
• Words like "Envy," "Empathy," and "Sympathy" have entirely different meanings and do not convey hatred or dislike.
</ul
